info.title: Dataverse Web API (admin subset)
info.description:
Unofficial, and deliberately partial.

The Dataverse Web API is the per-environment OData v4 endpoint at `https://{organization}.crm{n}.dynamics.com/api/data/v9.2/`. Every table in every environment is addressable through it and the model differs per environment, so a complete document is neither possible nor useful. **This is a curated admin/ALM subset** — the operation surface an infrastructure client actually uses: table definitions, generic record CRUD and query, relationship manipulation, solutions and solution import, environment variables, publishers, users and security roles, and organization settings. For the full per-environment model, fetch that environment's own CSDL at `GET /api/data/v9.2/$metadata`, which is authoritative and machine-readable; Microsoft Learn documents the same surface in prose.

Derived from the wire behaviour encoded in microsoft/terraform-provider-power-platform's client (`internal/clients/dataverse`) and then **probed against a live tenant**. Envelope and annotation shapes, paging and count behaviour, option-set values, api-version routing and error bodies were all confirmed against a real environment; those operations carry `x-probe-verified: true`. Operations that mutate solutions, settings or users are marked `x-probe-verified: false` — they are documented from the client and from public behaviour, not from a live write.

## Host and audience

The host is per environment, so `servers` carries a placeholder. Resolve the real one from the admin APIs — BAPI's environment record, or the `instanceApiUrl` of the Power Platform API's environment resource — rather than deriving it from an environment id. The OAuth audience is the environment's own URL, so the scope is `https://{host}/.default`. (A token minted for one environment was observed to be accepted by a sibling environment in the same tenant. Do not build on that; mint per host.)

## Conventions that hold everywhere

Stated once here rather than repeated on every operation.

- **Collection names route, logical names do not.** Records live under the table's `EntitySetName` (`accounts`), while callers usually hold the logical name (`account`). Resolve one to the other through `EntityDefinitions` before building a URL.
- **Envelope.** Collections return `@odata.context`, `value`, and `@odata.nextLink` when truncated. Single records return the row itself with a `/$entity` context and no wrapper. Function results return neither — their context ends in `#Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.<Name>Response`. Every row carries `@odata.etag`.
- **Lookups are asymmetric.** Read `_{navProperty}_value`; write `{navProperty}@odata.bind` with a relative URL; filter on the `_…_value` shadow with the guid unquoted.
- **Creates answer with an empty body** and put the new id in the `OData-EntityId` header. `Prefer: return=representation` swaps that for the row itself, echoed in `Preference-Applied`.
- **PATCH upserts.** A PATCH against an id that does not exist creates the record; `If-Match: *` makes it update-only.
- **Counts saturate at 5000.** Both `@odata.count` and `@Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.totalrecordcount` cap there, with `@Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.totalrecordcountlimitexceeded: true` as the signal.
- **Metadata endpoints are not entity sets.** `EntityDefinitions` and its children accept `$top` and ignore it, and never page.
- **Errors** are `{"error":{"code","message"}}` with a hexadecimal `code`. Messages are localized and interpolated; match on codes. Two failures escape that envelope: a 401 has an empty body and reports itself in headers, and a request with no api-version segment answers `{"Message": "..."}` from below the OData layer.
- **Throttling** is per user per environment over a rolling five-minute window, so parallelising a job across records makes 429s more likely rather than less.

## API versions

`v9.0`, `v9.1` and `v9.2` all route and, for the operations here, answer identically — the segment selects the CSDL a client validates against rather than different behaviour. Paths are pinned to the version the provider uses in the field: `v9.2` throughout, except `RetrieveSolutionImportResult`, `RetrieveSettingList()`, `SaveSettingValue()` and `organizations`, which it calls on `v9.0`. `v9.3` is not served.

servers.description: The environment's own Dataverse host. Resolve it from the admin APIs; it is not derivable from an environment id.

tags.name: Identity
tags.description: Resolving a bearer token to the Dataverse user, business unit and organization it maps to inside one environment.

tags.name: Table Definitions
tags.description: The metadata surface: the tables of an environment's model, their columns and their relationships. Reading only — authoring schema is outside this spec's scope. This is where a generic client learns the collection names, primary keys and navigation properties every other operation needs.

tags.name: Records
tags.description: Generic record CRUD and OData query against any table, addressed by its collection name. One set of operations covers every table in the environment, custom ones included.

tags.name: Relationships
tags.description: Reading and changing the links between records: `@odata.bind` for single-valued lookups, and the `$ref` collection for collection-valued relationships such as a user's security roles.

tags.name: Solutions
tags.description: The inventory of solutions installed in an environment, and their removal. A solution is the unit in which customizations are packaged and moved between environments.

tags.name: Solution Import
tags.description: Getting a solution package into an environment: staging and validating it, starting the import or in-place upgrade, polling the system job, and reading the verdict. Completion and success are deliberately separate questions here.

tags.name: Environment Variables
tags.description: Environment variables: definitions, which ship inside solutions and carry a default, and values, which are the per-environment overrides. The mechanism by which one solution package behaves differently in dev, test and production.

tags.name: Publishers
tags.description: Solution publishers — the identity that owns solutions and stamps its customization prefix onto every component they create.

tags.name: Users and Roles
tags.description: Interactive and application users, the security roles granted to them, and the business units both are scoped to. Everything here is per environment: a user's identity, their roles, and the roles themselves all differ between environments.

tags.name: Organization Settings
tags.description: Environment-level configuration, which lives in two unrelated places: the very wide `organization` row, and a weakly-typed list of backend feature switches beside it.

get.description: Resolves the bearer token to the Dataverse user, business unit and organization of this environment. The cheapest way to confirm a token is accepted by a given host, and to obtain the organization id without reading the 500-column `organizations` row.

200.description: The caller's identity in this environment.

get.description:
Lists the tables of this environment's model. Filtering on `LogicalCollectionName` is how a caller inverts a plural collection name back to a table's singular logical name.

Metadata endpoints are not ordinary entity sets: `$top`, `$count` and `$orderby` are accepted and then silently ignored, only `$select` and `$filter` have effect, and there is no paging — the whole collection arrives in one response.

200.description: Every table matching the filter, unpaged.

get.description:
Reads one table's metadata by logical name. Without `$select` the response carries around 115 properties; `$select=PrimaryIdAttribute,LogicalCollectionName` is the pair every generic record operation needs first, because the Web API routes on the *collection* name (`accounts`) while callers usually hold the *logical* name (`account`).

Expanding the three relationship collections returns the metadata that resolves a navigation property to the table on its other end. They do not share a shape: one-to-many and many-to-one entries describe the relationship as Referenced/Referencing, while many-to-many entries describe it symmetrically as Entity1/Entity2. The same relationship appears in `ManyToOneRelationships` of the referencing table and in `OneToManyRelationships` of the referenced table, so both carry `RelationshipType: OneToManyRelationship`.

200.description: The table's metadata.

get.description:
Every attribute (column) of a table. Entries are polymorphic: an `@odata.type` discriminator names the concrete metadata subtype, and is absent on rows of the plain base type — the shadow `…name` columns that accompany option sets, for instance — so a client cannot assume it is always present.

Casting the collection to a concrete subtype exposes the properties only that subtype has. `Attributes(LogicalName='statuscode')/Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.StatusAttributeMetadata?$expand=OptionSet($select=Options)` is the authoritative way to read an option set's real values and labels rather than guessing them.

As on the rest of the metadata surface, `$top` is ignored and the response is unpaged.

200.description: Every column of the table, unpaged.

get.description:
The generic OData read against any table's collection name.

Paging is server-driven: the default page is 5000 rows and `Prefer: odata.maxpagesize=N` lowers it. Follow `@odata.nextLink` verbatim — it carries an opaque `$skiptoken` paging cookie, and `$skip` is not a substitute for it.

`$count=true` adds `@odata.count`; the `odata.include-annotations` preference adds the two CRM count annotations. Both saturate at 5000, so on a large table a count is a floor rather than a total — `@Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.totalrecordcountlimitexceeded` is the signal that it was capped.

`savedQuery` and `userQuery` run a stored system or personal view instead of an inline query; the view supplies its own column list, which then appears inside `@odata.context`.

200.description: One server-driven page of matching records.

post.description:
Creates one record from a flat map of column logical names to values.

Single-valued (lookup) relationships are set through the `@odata.bind` annotation on the **navigation property**, and writing the read-only `_{navProperty}_value` shadow column instead is rejected. The navigation property is frequently *not* spelled like the lookup column: `environmentvariablevalue`'s lookup column is `environmentvariabledefinitionid` while its navigation property is `EnvironmentVariableDefinitionId`, and binding to the column name is refused as an undeclared property. Read the correct name from the table's relationship metadata (`ReferencingEntityNavigationPropertyName`) rather than assuming.

Collection-valued relationships cannot be set here at all; associate them afterwards through the relationship's `$ref` collection.

By default the new id comes back only in a response header. `Prefer: return=representation` swaps that for the created row.

201.description: Created, and the row is returned because the request carried `Prefer: return=representation`.

OData-EntityId.description: Absolute URL of the affected record. On a create with an empty body this is where the new id appears; parse the trailing `({id})`.

Location.description: The same URL as `OData-EntityId`, sent alongside it on every create and update observed. Either header can be read; the pair is redundant rather than complementary.

Preference-Applied.description: Echo of the `Prefer` values the service honoured. A preference it does not support is dropped silently and does not appear here.

204.description: Created. The body is empty and the new record's id is in `OData-EntityId`. This is the default; ask for the row itself with `Prefer: return=representation`.

OData-EntityId.description: Absolute URL of the affected record. On a create with an empty body this is where the new id appears; parse the trailing `({id})`.

Location.description: The same URL as `OData-EntityId`, sent alongside it on every create and update observed. Either header can be read; the pair is redundant rather than complementary.

412.description: A record with the same alternate-key values already exists (`0x80040237`). A caller doing create-or-update can treat this as the signal to switch to a PATCH — but it must have the record's primary key to address one, which a create response never gave it.

get.description: Reads one record by primary key. Unlike a query this returns the row itself: `@odata.context` ends in `/$entity` and there is no `value` wrapper.

200.description: The record.

patch.description:
Updates the named columns and leaves the rest alone.

PATCH against a key that does not exist is an **upsert**: the service creates the record with that id. `If-Match: *` forbids the create, making the request update-only; `If-None-Match: *` forbids the update, making it create-only. A caller that means "update" and sends neither will silently materialise a record when the id is wrong.

An etag in `If-Match` instead of `*` makes the write conditional on the row not having changed since it was read.

200.description: Updated, and the row is returned because the request carried `Prefer: return=representation`.

Preference-Applied.description: Echo of the `Prefer` values the service honoured. A preference it does not support is dropped silently and does not appear here.

204.description: Updated, or — when no record had that id and `If-Match` was absent — created by upsert. Empty body.

OData-EntityId.description: Absolute URL of the affected record. On a create with an empty body this is where the new id appears; parse the trailing `({id})`.

Location.description: The same URL as `OData-EntityId`, sent alongside it on every create and update observed. Either header can be read; the pair is redundant rather than complementary.

Preference-Applied.description: Echo of the `Prefer` values the service honoured. A preference it does not support is dropped silently and does not appear here.

delete.description:
Deletes one record.

Collection-valued relationships are not detached automatically, and a relationship whose cascade configuration sets `Delete: Restrict` blocks the delete while a related record exists — disassociate through the `$ref` collection first.

204.description: Deleted.

get.description:
Traverses a collection-valued navigation property and returns the related rows themselves. `@odata.context` names the *related* table, not the one the traversal started from.

`$select` here is additive rather than exclusive: the related table's primary key and `@odata.etag` come back whether or not they were selected.

200.description: The related records.

get.description: Returns entity references rather than rows: each entry is a lone `@odata.id` absolute URL. This is the cheap read for reconciling a desired relationship set against the current one — compare `@odata.id` strings, then add what is missing and remove the rest.

200.description: The relationship's current references.

post.description:
Adds one entry to a collection-valued relationship. The body is a single `@odata.id` holding the **absolute** URL of the record to attach; a relative path is rejected outright rather than resolved against the request URL.

Adding a pair that is already related was observed to be accepted as a no-op, so a reconciling caller need not diff first — though it still should, to avoid the round trips.

204.description: Associated.

delete.description:
Removes one entry from a collection-valued relationship, naming the other end through the `$id` query parameter as an absolute URL. This is the form the security-role assignment surface uses.

A `$id` naming a record that does not exist is reported as a missing record, not as a missing relationship — the service resolves the target before checking whether the two are related.

204.description: Disassociated.

delete.description: The keyed alternative to removing through `$id`: the related record is addressed in the path instead of the query string. Identical in effect; both forms are accepted for collection-valued relationships.

204.description: Disassociated.

get.description:
Lists the solutions installed in this environment.

`$filter=isvisible eq true` hides the internal solutions the platform keeps for its own bookkeeping; omitting the filter gives everything actually installed, which is what a drift check wants. `$expand=publisherid` inlines the owning publisher row instead of leaving only its lookup shadow.

Match on `uniquename`: `solutionid` is regenerated when a solution is re-imported, so it is not stable across environments.

200.description: The matching solutions.

get.description:
Reads one solution by id. Callers holding only a unique name should query the collection with a filter instead, since `solutionid` differs per environment.

An unmanaged solution can also be created directly as a record — `POST /solutions` with `uniquename`, `friendlyname`, `version` and a publisher bound through `publisherid@odata.bind` — which is how a container is made before components are added to it. Importing a package is the other route, and the only one for managed solutions.

200.description: The solution.

delete.description:
Uninstalls a solution.

What this removes depends on the solution's managed flag: deleting a *managed* solution deletes its components and the data in them, while deleting an *unmanaged* solution removes only the container and leaves the components behind in the environment. A solution another installed solution depends on cannot be deleted until the dependent one is.

204.description: Deleted.

post.description:
Uploads a base64-encoded solution `.zip` and validates it **without importing anything**.

The outcome is not in the status code — a package that cannot be imported still returns a success status, and the verdict lives in `StageSolutionResults.StageSolutionStatus`. Only `Passed` means importable; `MissingDependencies` and `SolutionValidationResults` say why it is not.

On success `StageSolutionUploadId` is the handle passed to the import or upgrade call, and `SolutionDetails` reports the unique name, friendly name, version and managed flag read out of the package — the only way to learn what a package contains before committing to importing it.

Staging is idempotent and safe to repeat, each time yielding a fresh upload id. Uploads expire, so stage and import within the same run.

200.description: The staging verdict — **pass or fail**. A package that cannot be imported arrives here, not as an error status: check `StageSolutionResults.StageSolutionStatus`, and expect `StageSolutionUploadId` to be all zeros and every `SolutionDetails` property to be null when it failed.

400.description: The request itself was malformed — most often the `CustomizationFile` parameter missing altogether, reported as `0x80048d19`. A *bad* package is not a 400; it comes back as a failed staging result with a 200.

post.description:
Starts the asynchronous import of a package already staged.

Two correlation ids come back and both are needed: `AsyncOperationId` addresses the system job to poll for completion, and `ImportJobKey` addresses the import job whose result carries the actual verdict. Completion and success are separate questions — a job can complete having failed.

**Not idempotent.** A retry after an ambiguous transport failure starts a second import. Send it exactly once, then reconcile by polling.

`ComponentParameters` supplies deployment settings — connection references and environment variable values — each entry discriminated by an `@odata.type` naming the table it targets. Omit the property entirely rather than sending an empty array.

200.description: The import has been **started**, not completed. Poll the system job named by `AsyncOperationId`, then read the verdict with `ImportJobKey`.

400.description: The request was refused before any job started. An unknown or expired `StageSolutionUploadId` — including the all-zeros value a failed staging returns — reports `0x8004f066`.

post.description:
The upgrade counterpart of the import call, taking the same request body and returning the same pair of correlation ids.

Where the import installs, this imports the package as a staged upgrade of an existing managed install and then applies it, deleting components the new version dropped. It requires the target solution to be already installed and managed.

Carries the same non-idempotency warning: send once, then poll.

200.description: The upgrade has been **started**, not completed. Poll as for an import.

get.description:
Reads the system job behind a long-running operation. Solution imports, upgrades, exports and publish-all jobs all report here.

A non-null `completedon` is the cheapest test that the job has finished, equivalent to `statecode` reaching Completed. **Finished is not the same as succeeded**: `statuscode` carries the outcome, and for a solution import the authoritative verdict is the import job result rather than this row.

This is an ordinary table, so `$select` works and a caller can narrow the 52-column row to the four fields it polls. There is no `Retry-After` and no dedicated operation-status endpoint, so the polling interval is the caller's to choose.

200.description: The system job's current state.

get.description:
Reads the verdict of an import job, keyed by the `ImportJobKey` the import or upgrade call returned. This — not the system job's status — is what decides whether an import succeeded.

Pinned to `v9.0` because that is what the provider calls in the field. It answers identically under `v9.2`; the version segment is not load-bearing here.

200.description: The import job's result. `SolutionOperationResult.Status` is the verdict; the message arrays carry the detail.

post.description:
Promotes every unpublished customization in the environment to its published state. The body is an empty JSON object.

Synchronous from the caller's point of view — it hands back no async operation id — but on a large environment it runs for minutes and may time out at the gateway while the work continues server-side. It is safe to re-run, and a matching `PublishAll` system job is visible in `asyncoperations` while it runs.

204.description: Every pending customization is published.

get.description:
Lists the environment variable definitions present in this environment.

Definitions are solution components: they ship inside a solution package and declare a variable's schema name, type and default. Filter on `schemaname`, the publisher-prefixed identifier that deployment settings files key on; an embedded apostrophe is escaped by doubling it.

A definition alone has no environment-specific value — `defaultvalue` applies until a value row overrides it.

200.description: The matching definitions.

get.description:
Lists the per-environment overrides.

Find the value belonging to a definition by filtering on the lookup's read-only shadow column, `_environmentvariabledefinitionid_value`, with the guid unquoted as all guid comparisons are. At most one value row exists per definition; an empty result means the definition is still on its default, which is not an error.

200.description: The matching value rows. An empty `value` array means no override is set.

post.description:
Creates the value row that overrides a definition's default.

The definition is attached through `EnvironmentVariableDefinitionId@odata.bind` — the **navigation property**, which is cased differently from the `environmentvariabledefinitionid` lookup column and is not interchangeable with it. `value` is always a string whatever the definition's declared type — a Number variable takes `"42"`, a Boolean takes `"true"` or `"false"` — and the service does not coerce or validate it against the type here.

get.description: Lists the solution publishers of this environment. Without `$select` each row carries 66 columns, most of them two unused address blocks. Filter on `uniquename` to look one up by name, doubling an embedded apostrophe to escape it.

200.description: The matching publishers.

post.description:
Creates a solution publisher.

`uniquename`, `friendlyname` and `customizationprefix` are the meaningful inputs. The prefix is stamped onto the schema name of every component the publisher's solutions create and cannot be changed once any exist, so it is effectively permanent. `customizationoptionvalueprefix` reserves the option-value range for those same components; omitting it lets the service allocate one.

`uniquename` is unique per environment and a collision is refused outright rather than resolved — there is no upsert on this path.

get.description:
Lists the users of this environment. The table holds both interactive users and application (service principal) users; `applicationid` is non-null only on the latter.

Two filters carry identity resolution: `azureactivedirectoryobjectid` for an interactive user just granted access, and `applicationid` for an application user. Both lag their upstream grant — a freshly added user is invisible here for tens of seconds — so an empty result means "not yet", and callers should poll rather than conclude absence.

Deleted users are soft-deleted rather than removed, so filter on `deletedstate` or a delete-then-recreate cycle looks like a duplicate.

Expanding `systemuserroles_association` inlines the assigned security roles. That expansion is itself paged: watch for a `systemuserroles_association@odata.nextLink` sibling of the inlined array when a user has many roles.

200.description: The matching users.

post.description:
Registers an Entra service principal as a Dataverse application user.

The request needs only the application id, the non-interactive access mode and a business unit binding; name and domain name are filled in by the service from the Entra registration. The service principal must already exist in the tenant.

A new application user has no security roles and therefore no data access at all until roles are assigned.

200.description: The user.

patch.description:
Updates a user.

`isdisabled` toggles access, and on an application user the patch must carry `applicationid` alongside it. Moving a user between business units through `businessunitid@odata.bind` silently drops every security role scoped to the old unit, because roles are per business unit — re-assign afterwards.

delete.description:
Removes a user, in two passes.

The first delete **soft-deletes**: the row survives with `deletedstate` set to soft-deleted and stops consuming a licence. Issuing the same delete a second time removes it permanently. A caller that wants the row genuinely gone must run both, and expect the second pass to find nothing once it has succeeded.

204.description: Deleted — soft-deleted on the first pass, permanently on the second.

get.description: Lists a user's assigned security roles as bare references. Cheaper than expanding the association when only the set of role ids matters.

200.description: References to the user's assigned roles.

post.description:
Assigns one security role to a user. There is no batch form outside `$batch`, so assigning several roles means several requests with no atomicity across them.

The `@odata.id` must be an absolute URL on the same environment host. A role id that does not exist is reported as a missing `role` record (`0x80040217`) rather than as a relationship error — worth knowing, because clients that special-case the generic unresolvable-reference code `0x80060888` here will not match it.

204.description: The role is assigned.

delete.description: Removes one security role from a user, naming the role through `$id` as an absolute URL. One role per request, as for assignment.

204.description: The role is no longer assigned.

get.description:
Lists the security roles of this environment.

Roles exist **per business unit**: the same role name appears once for every unit, each with its own `roleid`. Resolving a role by name therefore needs a business unit filter as well, or the match is ambiguous — and assigning a role from the wrong unit fails.

200.description: The matching roles.

get.description: Lists business units. Filtering on a null parent selects the root unit, of which there is always exactly one — the anchor for creating application users and for scoping role lookups.

200.description: The matching business units.

get.description:
Reads the environment's organization row.

There is exactly one, and it is the widest row on the API — 500 columns on a stock environment, holding audit configuration, attachment limits, IP firewall rules and feature toggles as ordinary columns. Always `$select`; reading it whole moves a great deal of data to answer a question about one flag.

`organizationid` from this row is the key the update needs, since the row cannot be patched through the collection.

200.description: A `value` array holding exactly one organization row.

patch.description:
Changes environment settings, one column at a time.

The row must be addressed by key; PATCH against the `organizations` collection is not allowed.

Send only the columns being changed. **Read-only columns are accepted and silently discarded** rather than refused — patching `name` returns success and changes nothing — so a caller that round-trips the whole 500-column row gets a misleading success. Verify by reading back.

Several settings interact: the audit sub-switches do nothing while the master switch is off, and the IP firewall's enforcing mode will lock out every caller including this one if the allowed range is wrong, so validate a range in audit mode first. Some columns are also one-way — `auditretentionperiodv2` cannot be set back to null once it holds a value; use `-1` (retain forever) instead.

204.description: Applied — but only for the columns that are writable. Read-only columns in the payload were discarded without comment, so success here does not prove the value changed.

400.description: The change was refused. A value outside a choice column's range reports `0x8004431a` and the message lists the accepted values; a column that cannot be null reports `0x80040200`; a property that is not on the type at all reports `0x80048d19`. Note that a merely *implausible* value in a writable numeric column is accepted rather than clamped.

500.description: An internal failure. The provider treats a 500 from this operation as a settings validation failure and surfaces its body rather than retrying, because older platform versions reported refusals this way.

get.description:
Reads the *other* settings surface: the weakly-typed bag of feature switches — "OrgDB org settings" — that the organization row does not model as columns. Around 112 entries on a stock environment, and the set differs per environment and grows with each platform release.

Every value is a string; the entry's data type says how to read it. A setting absent from the list has never been set in this environment and is running on its server-side default, so absence is not the same as false.

This is a function result rather than a collection: no `value` array, no paging, and query options do not apply — the whole list comes back or none of it does.

200.description: Every backend setting that has a value in this environment. Settings never set are simply absent.

post.description:
Writes one backend setting.

There is no batch form, so a caller changing several settings issues one request per setting and is not protected against a partial apply when a later one fails. `Value` is a string regardless of the setting's data type, but the service does type-check it against the setting's declared type before storing.

204.description: The setting is saved.

400.description: The write was refused: `0x81000067` when no setting exists with that name — names are case-sensitive and are not created on demand — or `0x81000068` when the value cannot be converted to the setting's declared data type. Both are client errors; do not retry.

500.description: An internal failure. The provider treats a 500 from this operation as a settings validation failure and surfaces its body, because older platform versions reported refusals here rather than as a 400.

entra_auth.description: Microsoft Entra ID OAuth2. The audience is the environment's own URL, so the scope is per environment — `https://{organizationHost}/.default`. A 401 advertises both the authority and the expected audience in its `WWW-Authenticate` header, which is the reliable way to discover them.

scopes.https://{organizationHost}/.default: Full access to one environment's Dataverse Web API as the signed-in user.

apiVersion.name: apiVersion
apiVersion.description: Web API version segment. `v9.2` is current and what generic clients use; `v9.0` and `v9.1` remain routable and answer identically for the operations here — the segment selects the CSDL a client validates against, not different behaviour.

logicalName.name: logicalName
logicalName.description: Singular logical name of the table, always lower case. Not the collection name that record URLs use.

entitySetName.name: entitySetName
entitySetName.description: The table's `EntitySetName` / `LogicalCollectionName`, which is what the Web API routes on — not the singular logical name. Resolve one from the other through the table definitions when only the logical name is held.

recordId.name: recordId
recordId.description: Primary key of the record: a bare guid, without braces and without quotes.

relatedRecordId.name: relatedRecordId
relatedRecordId.description: Primary key of the record on the other end of the relationship.

navigationProperty.name: navigationProperty
navigationProperty.description: The relationship's navigation property as it appears in the table's relationship metadata — `ReferencedEntityNavigationPropertyName`, `ReferencingEntityNavigationPropertyName`, or `Entity1`/`Entity2NavigationPropertyName` for many-to-many. It is **not** the relationship's `SchemaName`, which frequently differs.

solutionId.name: solutionId
solutionId.description: Primary key of the solution. Regenerated when a solution is re-imported, so it is not stable across environments — `uniquename` is.

organizationId.name: organizationId
organizationId.description: From the organization row's `organizationid`; there is no other way to obtain it except `WhoAmI`.

asyncOperationId.name: asyncOperationId
asyncOperationId.description: The `AsyncOperationId` handed back when the long-running operation was started.

importJobId.name: importJobId
importJobId.description: The `ImportJobKey` returned when the import was started. Written unquoted inside the function's parentheses, unlike a string function argument.

select.name: $select
select.description: Comma-separated column logical names. Exclusive on record reads; on a navigation-property traversal it is additive, and the related table's primary key and `@odata.etag` come back regardless.

filter.name: $filter
filter.description: OData filter expression. Guid comparisons are written **unquoted**; string comparisons are quoted, with an embedded apostrophe escaped by doubling it. Lookup columns are filtered through their read-only `_{navProperty}_value` shadow, never through the navigation property itself.

top.name: $top
top.description: Maximum rows to return. Honoured on entity sets; **accepted and ignored on the `EntityDefinitions` metadata surface**, which always returns everything.

expand.name: $expand
expand.description: Navigation properties to inline, each optionally with its own nested `$select`. An expanded collection can itself be paged — a `{navProperty}@odata.nextLink` sibling of the inlined array means the expansion was truncated.

expandRelationships.name: $expand
expandRelationships.description: Relationship metadata collections to inline. Each is expensive: expanding all three on a stock table returns dozens of fully-detailed relationship objects.

expandOptionSet.name: $expand
expandOptionSet.description: Expand an attribute's option set. Only meaningful once the collection has been cast to a concrete metadata subtype that has one.

count.name: $count
count.description: Adds `@odata.count` to the response envelope. The count saturates at 5000 on large tables.

apply.name: $apply
apply.description: OData aggregation. Results arrive inside the ordinary `value` array, padded with null managed-property columns (`canbedeleted`, `iscustomizable`) that were never asked for.

savedQuery.name: savedQuery
savedQuery.description: Run a stored **system** view instead of an inline query. The view supplies the column list, which is reflected in `@odata.context`. Mutually exclusive with `userQuery`.

userQuery.name: userQuery
userQuery.description: Run a stored **personal** view. Mutually exclusive with `savedQuery`.

refId.name: $id
refId.description: Absolute URL of the record on the other end of the relationship. Must be absolute and on the same environment host.

preferHeader.name: Prefer
preferHeader.description:
OData preferences, comma-separated. Three matter on this API:

- `return=representation` — make a create or update answer with the affected row instead of an empty body.
- `odata.maxpagesize=N` — lower the 5000-row server-driven page size.
- `odata.include-annotations="…totalrecordcount,…totalrecordcountlimitexceeded"` — add the CRM count annotations to a collection response.

Whatever the service honoured is echoed back in `Preference-Applied`; anything it does not support is dropped without complaint.

ifMatch.name: If-Match
ifMatch.description: `*` forbids the upsert-create on PATCH, making the request update-only. An etag value instead makes the write conditional on the row not having changed since it was read.

ifNoneMatch.name: If-None-Match
ifNoneMatch.description: `*` forbids the update on PATCH, making the request create-only.

400.description: Bad request, and a client bug rather than a transient failure. An unknown column in `$select` or `$filter` reports `0x80060888`; a payload that will not deserialize — a missing action parameter, an undeclared property, a relative URI where an absolute one was required — reports `0x80048d19`; a missing required column or an all-zeros guid reports `0x80040203`; a value outside a choice column's range reports `0x8004431a` and the message lists the accepted values.

401.description: Unauthorized. The body is **empty** — the reason is in the headers. `WWW-Authenticate` names both the authority to authenticate against and the audience to request a token for, which is the environment's own URL.

WWW-Authenticate.description: `Bearer authorization_uri=…, resource_id=https://{host}/`. The `resource_id` is the scope to request.

401_error_reason.description: Non-standard Dataverse header spelling out the failure, e.g. a missing or malformed `Authorization` header.

403.description: Forbidden. The token is valid but the Dataverse user it maps to lacks the privilege for this operation — or has no user row in this environment at all, which is the usual cause for a service principal that was never registered as an application user.

404.description: Not found, reported as `0x80040217` when a record, function argument or reference target does not exist — the entity name and id are quoted in the message — and as `0x80060888` when a URL segment or property is not part of the model at all. Three cases surface here that a caller might expect elsewhere: a delete against a record that is already gone, a PATCH carrying `If-Match: *` against a record that does not exist, and an association whose target record does not exist.

405.description: The method is not allowed on this resource — most commonly a PATCH aimed at a collection rather than at a keyed record. The error envelope is present but its `code` is the **empty string**.

412.description: Precondition failed. `If-None-Match: *` against an existing record reports `0x80040237` ("a record with matching key values already exists"); a stale etag in `If-Match` reports `0x80060882`. Note that `If-Match: *` against a **missing** record answers 404 rather than 412.

429.description: Throttled by service protection limits, which count requests, execution time and concurrency per user per environment over a rolling five-minute window. Because the limits are per user, fanning work out across records makes throttling **more** likely, not less. Honour `Retry-After` rather than backing off on a schedule of your own.

501.description: The `apiVersion` segment names a Web API version this environment does not serve, reported as `0x8006088a`. `v9.3` and above are not available.

ODataContext.description: Absolute URL of this environment's `$metadata` document with a fragment naming what came back: `#solutions` for a collection, `#solutions(publisherid())` when expanded, `#accounts(<id>)/$entity` for a single record, `#Collection($ref)` for a reference collection, and `#Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.<Name>Response` for a function or action result. Splitting the fragment at the first `(` or `/` yields the collection name the response came from, which is how a generic client recovers a table name it did not know.

ODataError.description: The error envelope of every Dataverse Web API failure that reaches the OData layer. Two failures do not use it: a 401, whose body is empty, and a request with no api-version segment, which answers with the pre-OData shape instead.

ODataErrorBody.description: The failure itself. Only `code` is worth matching on.

code.description:
Hexadecimal Dataverse status code, as a string. Stable across locales and platform versions, unlike the message, and the only part of the error worth matching on. Observed on this surface:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0x80040200` | A required column was set to null on update. |
| `0x80040203` | A required column was missing, or an argument was invalid — including an all-zeros guid. |
| `0x80040217` | The record, function argument or reference target does not exist. |
| `0x80040237` | A record with matching key values already exists. |
| `0x8004431a` | A value is outside a choice column's valid range; the message lists the accepted values. |
| `0x80044331` | A uniqueness constraint was violated, such as a duplicate publisher unique name. |
| `0x80048d19` | The request payload could not be deserialized — a missing action parameter, an undeclared property, or a relative URI where an absolute one was required. |
| `0x8004f066` | The staged solution upload id is not valid or has expired. |
| `0x80060882` | The etag in `If-Match` does not match the stored row version. |
| `0x80060888` | A URL segment, property or entity reference is not part of the model. |
| `0x8006088a` | The requested api-version is not served. |
| `0x81000067` | No backend setting exists with that name. |
| `0x81000068` | A backend setting value could not be converted to the setting's data type. |

Some transport-level failures — a method not allowed on a resource, for instance — return this envelope with `code` set to the **empty string**, so a client must tolerate that rather than assume a code is always present.

message.description: Human-readable, **localized**, and interpolated with entity names and ids. Never parse it; match on `code` instead.
message.example: Entity 'account' With Id = 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 Does Not Exist

@Microsoft.PowerApps.CDS.ErrorDetails.Op.description: Present on some platform-level errors; carries a secondary status the plugin pipeline attached.

innererror.description: Present on unhandled server-side faults. Carries a stack trace in non-production configurations, so it should not be surfaced to end users.

NonODataError.description: The shape of failures rejected **before** the OData layer sees them — notably a request whose path carries no api-version segment. A client that unconditionally reads `error.code` finds nothing here.

Message.description: The whole failure. There is no code to match on.
Message.example: Requested API Version must be provided.  Please provide in the format /api/data/v<Major>.<Minor>/

WhoAmIResponse.description: The Dataverse identity a bearer token maps to in this environment.

UserId.description: The caller's `systemuserid` in this environment. A different guid from the Entra object id, and different again in every other environment.

BusinessUnitId.description: Business unit the caller's user row belongs to. Determines which security roles can be assigned to them.

OrganizationId.description: Identifies the environment's Dataverse organization. The key `organizations_update` needs.

EntityDefinition.description: One table's metadata. Around 115 properties without `$select`; listed here are the ones a generic client needs to build URLs and resolve relationships.

MetadataId.description: Identifies this metadata object, not the table's records.

LogicalName.description: Singular, always lower case. What callers usually hold.

SchemaName.description: Cased form of the logical name, used in solution component references.

LogicalCollectionName.description: Plural name. Equal to `EntitySetName` on every table observed.

EntitySetName.description: The OData entity set — **this is what routes record URLs**. Prefer it over `LogicalCollectionName` when they could differ.

PrimaryIdAttribute.description: Logical name of the primary key column. Needed to tell an update from a create when a caller supplies an untyped column map, since finding this column in the map means the record's identity is already known.

PrimaryNameAttribute.description: Logical name of the column used as the record's display label in lookups and views.

ObjectTypeCode.description: Legacy numeric entity type code. Still used by columns that store a table reference, such as `returnedtypecode` on a view.

OwnershipType.description: Who a record can belong to, which in turn determines which security-role privilege depths mean anything for this table.

TableType.description: Storage model. `Elastic` tables trade transactional guarantees and some OData constructs for scale; `Virtual` tables are backed by an external data source and are read-mostly.

IsCustomEntity.description: False on tables that ship with the platform.

IsManaged.description: True when the table arrived inside a managed solution and cannot be edited directly.

OneToManyRelationships.description: Present only under `$expand`. Relationships in which this table is the *referenced* (one) side.

ManyToOneRelationships.description: Present only under `$expand`. Relationships in which this table is the *referencing* (many) side. The same shape as `OneToManyRelationships`, down to carrying `RelationshipType: OneToManyRelationship`, because it is the same relationship seen from the other end.

ManyToManyRelationships.description: Present only under `$expand`. A different shape from the other two: symmetric Entity1/Entity2 naming rather than Referenced/Referencing.

EntityDefinitionCollection.description: A metadata collection. Unlike entity-set collections it carries no paging or count annotations, because the metadata surface never pages.

Label.description: A localizable metadata label. Read `UserLocalizedLabel` in preference to indexing `LocalizedLabels`; it is the entry matching the caller's language, resolved server-side.

LocalizedLabels.description: One entry per language provisioned in the environment. Empty on labels that were never given text.

LocalizedLabel.description: One language's text for a metadata label.

Label.description: The text. Can legitimately be the empty string.

LanguageCode.description: Windows LCID, e.g. 1033 for English (United States).

IsManaged.description: True when the label arrived in a managed solution.

MetadataId.description: Identifies this label, so it can be patched independently of its parent.

AttributeMetadata.description: One column's metadata. Polymorphic on `@odata.type`; without `$select` each row carries around 55 properties, and casting the collection to a concrete subtype exposes the properties only that subtype has.

@odata.type.description: Names the concrete metadata subtype. **Absent** on rows of the plain base type — the shadow `…name` columns that accompany option sets, for instance — so a client cannot assume it is present. Fifteen distinct subtypes appear on a stock `account` table.

LogicalName.description: The column name used in record payloads and OData query options.

SchemaName.description: Cased form of the logical name.

AttributeType.description: The column's type, mirroring the `@odata.type` subtype but always present.

IsCustomAttribute.description: False on columns that ship with the platform.

IsValidForCreate.description: False on columns the service computes; sending one in a create is rejected.

IsValidForUpdate.description: False on write-once columns. Together with `IsValidForCreate` this is how a generic client decides what it may put in a payload.

IsValidForRead.description: False on columns that exist in the model but are never returned.

AttributeMetadataCollection.description: Every column of one table. Unpaged, like the rest of the metadata surface.

value.description: The table's columns, ordered by logical name.

OptionSetMetadata.description: The set of values a choice column accepts. Reached by casting the attribute to its concrete metadata subtype and expanding — the authoritative source for a column's real values, rather than inferring them from data.

Name.description: Set name. Publisher-prefixed on custom global option sets.

IsGlobal.description: True when the set is shared between columns, so editing it affects every column that uses it.

Options.description: The permitted values with their labels.

OptionMetadata.description: One permitted value of a choice column.

Value.description: The integer stored in the record. Custom values are allocated inside the publisher's reserved option-value range.

OneToManyRelationshipMetadata.description: A one-to-many relationship, described from whichever side was asked. Note the absence of `Entity1LogicalName`/`Entity2LogicalName`: those exist only on many-to-many metadata, so code that reads them off a one-to-many entry finds nothing.

SchemaName.description: The relationship's own name. **Not** what goes in a navigation-property URL segment — use the navigation property names below.

RelationshipType.description: Always this value on both `OneToManyRelationships` and `ManyToOneRelationships` entries, since they are the same relationship viewed from opposite ends.

ReferencedEntity.description: Logical name of the table on the *one* side — the target of the lookup.

ReferencedAttribute.description: Usually the referenced table's primary key.

ReferencingEntity.description: Logical name of the table on the *many* side — the one holding the lookup column.

ReferencingAttribute.description: The lookup column itself. Its read shadow is `_{this}_value`.

ReferencedEntityNavigationPropertyName.description: URL segment for traversing from the one side to the collection of many. This is what goes in a `$ref` path.

ReferencingEntityNavigationPropertyName.description: URL segment for traversing from the many side to the single one, and the property name to set with `@odata.bind`.

IsHierarchical.description: True on a self-referential relationship that forms a hierarchy, which unlocks the `Above`/`Under` filter operators.

ManyToManyRelationshipMetadata.description: A many-to-many relationship, described symmetrically. Backed by a hidden intersect table that is not directly addressable.

SchemaName.description: The relationship's own name, not a URL segment.

Entity1LogicalName.description: One end. Which end is 1 and which is 2 is an implementation detail, not a direction.

IntersectEntityName.description: The hidden join table holding the pairs.

Entity1IntersectAttribute.description: Column of the intersect table holding Entity1's key.

Entity2IntersectAttribute.description: Column of the intersect table holding Entity2's key.

Entity1NavigationPropertyName.description: URL segment for traversing from Entity1 to Entity2. Frequently **identical** to `Entity2NavigationPropertyName`, so a client resolving a navigation property back to a table must compare the *other* end's logical name against the table it started from rather than matching on the property name alone.

Entity2NavigationPropertyName.description: URL segment for traversing from Entity2 to Entity1.

CascadeConfiguration.description: What happens to related records when an action is taken on the referenced one. `Delete: Restrict` is what makes a record undeletable while a related record exists, and `Cascade` is what makes deleting a parent silently delete children.

Assign.description: Applied when the referenced record's owner changes.

Delete.description: `RemoveLink` clears the lookup, `Cascade` deletes the children, `Restrict` blocks the delete.

Archive.description: Applied when the referenced record is archived to long-term retention.

Merge.description: Applied when the referenced record is merged into another.

Reparent.description: Applied when the referenced record moves to a different parent in a hierarchy.

Share.description: Applied when the referenced record is shared with a user or team.

RollupView.description: Whether related records appear in the referenced record's rollup views.

Record.description:
A row of any table: column logical names mapped to values, plus the OData annotations the service adds.

Conventions that hold on every table:

- **Lookups read and write differently.** Reading gives the read-only shadow `_{navProperty}_value` holding a guid. Writing uses `{navProperty}@odata.bind` with a *relative* URL, where `{navProperty}` is the relationship's `ReferencingEntityNavigationPropertyName` — often cased and spelled differently from the column, so it must be read from metadata rather than derived. Writing the `_…_value` column directly is rejected.
- **Annotations arrive on request.** `Prefer: odata.include-annotations="*"` adds, per column: `{column}@OData.Community.Display.V1.FormattedValue` (the display string — a choice column's label, a money column's currency-formatted amount, a date in the caller's locale), and on lookups `_{nav}_value@Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.lookuplogicalname` (the target table) and `_{nav}_value@Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.associatednavigationproperty` (the navigation property to bind to, which is the reliable way to discover it inline).
- **Choice columns read as integers**, with the label only in the formatted-value annotation.
- **Selecting a money column silently pulls in `_transactioncurrencyid_value`** and its annotations, whether or not it was asked for.
- **Dates are UTC ISO-8601** ending in `Z`, except date-only columns, which are `YYYY-MM-DD`.
- **Money columns** are accompanied by a `{column}_base` in the organization's base currency, maintained by the service.
- Optional columns with no value are returned as explicit `null` rather than omitted.

@odata.etag.description: Row version, formatted as a weak etag around the row's `versionnumber`. Pass it back in `If-Match` for an optimistic-concurrency write.

RecordCollection.description: One server-driven page of records, with the paging and count annotations the request asked for.

@odata.count.description: Present when `$count=true` was sent. **Saturates at 5000** — on a larger table this is a floor, not a total.

@odata.nextLink.description: Present when the result was truncated by the server-driven page size. Follow it verbatim; it carries an opaque `$skiptoken` paging cookie that cannot be reconstructed from `$skip`.

@Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.totalrecordcount.description: Present only when the `odata.include-annotations` preference asked for it. Saturates at 5000 like `@odata.count`.
True when the count above hit the 5000 cap, meaning the real total is larger and unknown. The only reliable way to tell a table of exactly 5000 rows from one of half a million.

value.description: The matching rows. Empty rather than absent when nothing matched.

Reference.description: An entity reference: a record identified by URL rather than by value. The body shape for adding an entry to a collection-valued relationship.

@odata.id.description: Absolute URL of the record, `https://{host}/api/data/{apiVersion}/{entitySet}({id})`. Must be absolute and on the same environment host — a relative path is rejected.

RoleReference.description: An entity reference pointing at a security role. The body for assigning a role to a user.

@odata.id.description: Absolute URL of the role. The role must belong to the same business unit as the user, or it cannot be resolved.

ReferenceCollection.description: A collection of entity references. Its `@odata.context` is `…/$metadata#Collection($ref)` and does **not** name the related table, so a caller reconciling references must parse the entity set out of each `@odata.id`.

Solution.description: A row of the `solutions` table: one installed solution. 34 columns in full; the ALM-relevant ones are listed.

@odata.etag.description: Row version as a weak etag.

solutionid.description: Regenerated when the solution is re-imported, so it identifies an *installation*, not a solution. Match on `uniquename` across environments.

uniquename.description: The publisher-chosen identifier, stable across environments and re-imports. The right key for a drift check.

friendlyname.description: Display name, freely editable and not an identifier.

version.description: Usually four-part `major.minor.build.revision`, though platform solutions carry two-part values. Compared segment-by-segment as integers, not lexically.

ismanaged.description: True when the solution was imported as managed. Decides what deleting it removes: a managed delete takes the components and their data with it, an unmanaged delete leaves them behind.

isvisible.description: False on the internal solutions the platform maintains for its own bookkeeping. `$filter=isvisible eq true` is the list a human would recognise.

isapimanaged.description: True on solutions the service manages on the customer's behalf, which should not be edited by hand.

createdon.description: Travels with the package, so it is the same in every environment the solution is installed in.

installedon.description: When this environment received the solution — unlike `createdon`, environment-specific, and therefore what a deployment audit compares.

updatedon.description: When the installation was last upgraded in place. Null on a solution that has never been upgraded.

_publisherid_value.description: Read-only lookup shadow for the owning publisher. `$expand=publisherid` inlines the publisher row itself.

solutiontype.description: 0 on an ordinary solution. Non-zero values mark the specialised kinds the platform creates for itself.

_parentsolutionid_value.description: Non-null only on a patch: the solution this one patches.

versionnumber.description: Row version counter behind `@odata.etag`. Unrelated to the solution's `version`.

@odata.count.description: Present when `$count=true` was sent. **Saturates at 5000** — on a larger table this is a floor, not a total.

@odata.nextLink.description: Present when the result was truncated by the server-driven page size. Follow it verbatim; it carries an opaque `$skiptoken` paging cookie that cannot be reconstructed from `$skip`.

@Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.totalrecordcount.description: Present only when the `odata.include-annotations` preference asked for it. Saturates at 5000 like `@odata.count`.
True when the count above hit the 5000 cap, meaning the real total is larger and unknown. The only reliable way to tell a table of exactly 5000 rows from one of half a million.

value.description: The matching rows. Empty rather than absent when nothing matched.

StageSolutionRequest.description: A solution package offered for validation.

CustomizationFile.description: The solution `.zip`, base64-encoded. Standard base64, not the URL-safe alphabet. Large packages make this request body correspondingly large.

StageSolutionResponse.description: The envelope around a staging attempt. Always returned with a success status — the verdict is inside.

StageSolutionResults.description: What staging found: whether the package can be imported, and what it contains.

StageSolutionUploadId.description: Handle for the staged package, passed to the import or upgrade call. Expires after a while, so stage and import within one run. **All zeros when staging failed** — the sentinel for "no package was staged", and a value that will be rejected if passed on to an import.

StageSolutionStatus.description: The verdict. Only `Passed` means importable; anything else is a failure delivered inside a successful HTTP response, so check this explicitly.

SolutionValidationResults.description: Validation findings against the package itself — a malformed archive, a missing manifest, an unsupported export version. Empty on a package that passed.

MissingDependencies.description: Components the package needs that this environment does not have. The other common reason staging fails — install the solutions named in `RequiredSolutionName` first.

SolutionComponentsDetails.description: Component inventory read out of the package before anything is imported. Empty when staging failed early enough that the archive was never opened.

items.description: One component declared by the package.

SolutionValidationResult.description: One validation finding against a staged package.

SolutionValidationResultType.description: Severity of the finding. `Error` findings are what set `StageSolutionStatus` to `Failed`.

ErrorCode.description: Numeric code for the finding. A **signed 32-bit** value, typically large and negative — it is the same underlying code as an OData error's hexadecimal `code`, rendered as a signed integer rather than as a hex string, so `-2147188640` and `0x8004xxxx` are two spellings of one thing.

Message.description: Human-readable explanation. This is what to surface when staging fails.

MissingDependency.description: One unsatisfied dependency: a component the package needs (`Required…`) and the component inside the package that needs it (`Dependent…`).

RequiredComponentParentSchemaName.description: The table or parent component the missing component belongs to, e.g. the table owning a missing column.

RequiredComponentId.description: Identifies the missing component in the environment that does have it.

RequiredComponentType.description: Solution component type code, as a string.

RequiredSolutionName.description: The solution that would supply the missing component. Install it first.

DependentComponentSchemaName.description: The component in the package that needs it.

StageSolutionSolutionDetails.description: What the package declares about itself, alongside what the environment already has installed under the same name — the only way to know a package's identity, version and upgrade impact without importing it. Every property is null when staging failed before the archive could be read, so a caller must not assume this block is populated.

SolutionUniqueName.description: The unique name the solution will have once installed. Use it to read the installed solution back afterwards.

SolutionVersion.description: The version inside the package. Compare it against `PreviousSolutionVersion` to decide between an install and an upgrade, and to catch a downgrade.

IsManaged.description: Whether the package is managed. An in-place upgrade requires both this and `PreviousIsManaged` to be true.

IsPatchSolution.description: True when the package is a patch rather than a full solution. Patches layer on top of a base solution and cannot be imported without it.

PublisherUniqueName.description: Publisher declared inside the package. If it differs from `PreviousPublisherUniqueName` the import will fail or re-prefix components, so this is worth checking before importing.

PreviousSolutionUniqueName.description: What the environment already has installed under this name. Null when the solution is not yet installed, which is how an install is distinguished from an upgrade.

PreviousSolutionVersion.description: Version currently installed. Null on a first install.

PreviousIsManaged.description: Whether the installed copy is managed. Importing a managed package over an unmanaged install, or the reverse, is not an upgrade.

PreviousPublisherUniqueName.description: Publisher of the installed copy. A mismatch against `PublisherUniqueName` blocks the upgrade.

PreviousPatchSolutionsNames.description: Patches already applied on top of the installed solution. A base-solution upgrade will roll these up or invalidate them.

HasPendingUpgrade.description: True when a previous staged upgrade was imported but never applied. Staging another on top of it is likely to be rejected.

IsPrerequisitesExport.description: True when the package holds only prerequisite components rather than a complete solution.

IsCabFile.description: True when the upload is a `.cab` rather than a `.zip`. Legacy packaging.

ImportSolutionRequest.description: Instructions for importing or upgrading a package that has already been staged.

PublishWorkflows.description: Activate the package's flows and workflows as part of the import. When false they arrive deactivated and must be turned on afterwards.

OverwriteUnmanagedCustomizations.description: What to do about unmanaged customizations layered over the components being imported: `false` preserves them, so the environment's local edits survive; `true` discards them, so the package's definition wins. Preserving them can leave the environment behaving differently from the package.

SkipProductUpdateDependencies.description: Bypass the check that the environment's platform version satisfies the package's declared product dependencies. Useful when the dependency is declared too aggressively; risky otherwise.

ComponentParameters.description: Deployment settings applied during the import, each discriminated by `@odata.type`. **Omit the property entirely rather than sending an empty array** — an empty array is not equivalent.

StageSolutionUploadId.description: From the preceding staging call. An expired upload id fails the import.

ComponentParameter.description: A deployment-setting override applied during import, discriminated by `@odata.type`. These are what turn a portable package into a working install: without them, connection references arrive unbound and environment variables arrive on their defaults.

ConnectionReferenceParameter.description: Binds one of the package's connection references to an existing connection in this environment.

connectionreferencelogicalname.description: Must match the logical name declared inside the package; a mismatch leaves the reference unbound rather than failing.

connectionreferencedisplayname.description: Display name for the reference. Safe to leave empty.

connectionid.description: The connection to bind. It must already exist in this environment and be shared with the principal performing the import, or the flows using it will not run.

EnvironmentVariableParameter.description: Supplies the value for one of the package's environment variables at import time, instead of creating the value row separately afterwards.

schemaname.description: The variable's publisher-prefixed schema name, as declared in the package.

value.description: String-encoded regardless of the variable's declared type.

ImportSolutionResponse.description: The two handles a started import or upgrade hands back. Both are needed, because completion and success are answered by different endpoints.

AsyncOperationId.description: Key of the system job to poll for *completion*.

ImportJobKey.description: Key for reading the import job's *verdict*. A job can complete having failed, so this is the one that decides whether the import worked.

AsyncOperation.description: A row of the `asyncoperations` table: one long-running system job. 52 columns in full; the ones worth polling are listed.

name.description: Human-readable job name assigned by whatever started it.

operationtype.description: What kind of job this is. Relevant to solution work: 202 Export Solution, 203 Import Solution, 204 PublishAll, 207 DeleteAndPromote, 208 UninstallSolution, 211 StageAndUpgrade. The full set runs to well over a hundred values.

statecode.description: Coarse lifecycle state: 0 Ready (queued), 1 Suspended, 2 Locked (running), 3 Completed. Reaching 3 says the job stopped, not that it succeeded.

statuscode.description: Fine-grained status: 0 Waiting For Resources, 10 Waiting, 20 In Progress, 21 Pausing, 22 Canceling, 30 Succeeded, 31 Failed, 32 Canceled. This is where success or failure actually lives.

startedon.description: When a worker picked it up. Null while the job is still queued, which is how queue delay is distinguished from execution time.

completedon.description: Non-null exactly when the job has stopped, whatever the outcome. The cheapest completion test — no need to interpret `statecode`.

message.description: Failure detail, frequently a serialized server-side exception. Null on success.

friendlymessage.description: A user-facing summary of the failure, when the platform has one. Often null even on failures.

RetrieveSolutionImportResultResponse.description: The envelope around an import job's verdict.

SolutionOperationResult.description: The authoritative outcome of a solution import. Consulted after the system job completes, because a completed job can still have failed.

Status.description: `Passed` means the import succeeded. Anything else is a failure whose detail is in `ErrorMessages`.

ErrorMessages.description: Why the import failed. Empty on success. Entries are strings in practice but the service does not guarantee the element type.

WarningMessages.description: Non-fatal findings. Can be populated even when `Status` is `Passed`, and are worth surfacing.

EnvironmentVariableDefinition.description: A row of `environmentvariabledefinitions`: the *declaration* of an environment variable, shipped inside a solution. It carries the default, not the environment-specific value.

schemaname.description: Publisher-prefixed identifier that deployment settings files key on. The stable name across environments.

defaultvalue.description: Always a string, whatever `type` declares. Applies until a value row overrides it, so a variable with a default is never truly unset.

type.description: Declared type of the variable. It governs the maker experience and how consumers parse the string, but the API does **not** coerce or validate values against it: 100000000 String, 100000001 Number, 100000002 Boolean, 100000003 JSON, 100000004 Data Source, 100000005 Secret.

valueschema.description: JSON schema constraining permitted values, on the types that support one. Null when unconstrained.

secretstore.description: Where a Secret variable's value actually lives: 0 Azure Key Vault, 1 Microsoft Dataverse. Meaningful only when `type` is Secret; null or 0 on every other type.

EnvironmentVariableDefinitionCollection.description: A page of environment variable definitions.

domainname.description: UPN for an interactive user; a synthesised address for an application user. Not reliable as a cross-environment identifier.

applicationid.description: Entra application (client) id. **Non-null only on application users** — this is what distinguishes a service principal's user row from a person's.

azureactivedirectoryobjectid.description: Entra object id of the interactive user. Null on application users. The right filter for finding a person's user row after granting them access.

isdisabled.description: True blocks the user from the environment without removing them or their owned records.

deletedstate.description: 0 Not deleted, 1 Soft deleted. A deleted user's row survives at 1 until a second delete removes it, so filter on 0 or a delete-then-recreate cycle looks like a duplicate.

Organization.description: The single `organization` row — 500 columns on a stock environment, of which the ones the admin surface manipulates are listed. The rest are readable with `$select` and defined in the environment's CSDL.

organizationid.description: The key `organizationSettings_update` addresses; the row cannot be patched through the collection.

name.description: The organization's short name, fixed at provisioning.

_basecurrencyid_value.description: The base currency every money column's `_base` companion is expressed in. Chosen at provisioning and immutable.

maxuploadfilesize.description: Largest attachment accepted, in bytes. The platform caps this well below arbitrary values, and raising it does not raise the underlying file-storage limits.

blockedattachments.description: Semicolon-separated file extensions rejected as attachments, written **without leading dots**. Ships with a long default list of executable types; replacing the value replaces the whole list rather than adding to it.

plugintracelogsetting.description: How much plugin execution is written to the trace log: 0 Off, 1 Exception (only failed executions), 2 All. Anything but Off consumes storage, so All is a debugging setting rather than a steady state.

isauditenabled.description: Master audit switch. While false the two switches below have no effect, whatever they are set to, and no table-level audit configuration applies.

isuseraccessauditenabled.description: Records user sign-in and access events. Requires the master switch.

isreadauditenabled.description: Records read operations. By far the highest-volume audit category — enabling it on a busy environment generates a great deal of data. Requires the master switch.

auditretentionperiodv2.description: Days to retain audit records before the platform deletes them. `-1` means retain forever. Null until audit has ever been configured.

bounddashboarddefaultcardexpanded.description: Whether dashboard cards render expanded by default in model-driven apps.

iscustomcontrolsincanvasappsenabled.description: Allows Power Apps component framework components in canvas apps. Off by default because those components run with the app's privileges.

powerappsmakerbotenabled.description: Enables the Power Apps maker assistant for makers in this environment.

enableipbasedfirewallrule.description: **Enforcing** mode for the IP firewall: requests from outside the allowed ranges are refused. Turning this on with a wrong range locks out every caller including the one making the change — validate in audit mode first.

enableipbasedfirewallruleinauditmode.description: **Log-only** mode: out-of-range requests are recorded but still served. The safe way to confirm an allow-list is complete before enforcing it.

allowediprangeforfirewall.description: Comma-separated CIDR ranges permitted when the firewall is on. Empty or null with enforcement on means nothing is permitted.

allowedservicetagsforfirewall.description: Comma-separated Azure service tags permitted alongside the IP ranges, for callers whose addresses are not stable.

allowmicrosofttrustedservicetags.description: Lets Microsoft's own trusted services through the firewall. Turning it off can break first-party integrations that have no fixed address.

allowapplicationuseraccess.description: Whether application users bypass the IP firewall. Service principals frequently call from addresses that cannot be enumerated, so switching this off tends to break automation before it stops an attacker.

enableipbasedcookiebinding.description: Binds a session cookie to the IP address it was issued to, so a stolen cookie is unusable elsewhere. Can disrupt users behind rotating egress addresses.

reverseproxyipaddresses.description: Addresses of trusted reverse proxies whose forwarded-for headers the firewall should believe instead of the connecting address.

aipromptsenabled.description: Enables AI prompt features for makers in this environment.

paipreviewscenarioenabled.description: Opts the environment into preview AI scenarios, which are not covered by the usual service commitments.

blockaccesstosessiontranscriptsforcopilo.description: Prevents makers and admins from reading Copilot Studio conversation transcripts, independently of whether they are recorded.

blocktranscriptrecordingforcopilotstudio.description: Stops Copilot Studio conversations being recorded at all. Stronger than blocking access, and removes the data a maker would use to improve an agent.

enablecopilotstudiosharedatawithvivainsi.description: Shares Copilot Studio usage data with Viva Insights.

enablecopilotstudiocrossgeosharedatawith.description: Permits that sharing to cross a geographic boundary — a data-residency decision, not just a feature toggle.

SettingDetailCollection.description: One entry per setting that has ever been set here. Around 112 on a stock environment; the set differs per environment and grows with each platform release. A setting that is absent is running on its server-side default, which is not the same as being false.

SettingDetail.description: One backend ("OrgDB") setting: a weakly-typed feature switch that the organization row does not model as a column.
